h1: Sponsor licence for construction and engineering
title: Sponsor Licence for Construction & Engineering | 2026 Rules
description: Sponsor licence for construction and engineering firms: which trades and engineering roles can be sponsored in 2026, and the shortage list deadline.
intro: Construction and engineering employers can still sponsor overseas workers, but the rules for trades and for engineers are different. This page explains what a sponsor licence for construction allows in 2026, and the deadline you need to plan for.

sections.heading: Engineers and professional roles
sections.text: Professional engineering roles, such as civil, structural, mechanical and electrical engineers, quantity surveyors and project managers, are usually at degree level (RQF 6). They can still be sponsored if the salary rules are met: at least £41,700 a year, or the going rate for the job if higher.

sections.heading: Trades: the temporary shortage list
sections.text: Most construction trades are below degree level, so since July 2025 they can only be sponsored if the occupation is on the temporary shortage list. The interim list includes roles such as construction and building trades supervisors, painters and decorators, and floorers and wall tilers. Workers newly sponsored in these roles can't bring their partner or children as dependants.

sections.heading: The December 2026 deadline
sections.text: The interim temporary shortage list runs until 31 December 2026 unless it is extended. In July 2026, the Migration Advisory Committee recommended a shorter future list of 28 occupations, including construction and manufacturing trades and engineering technicians. The government's final decision will decide which trades can be sponsored from 2027, so plan any trade recruitment early.

sections.heading: Compliance on construction sites
sections.text: Construction is a priority sector for Home Office enforcement. Check the right to work of every worker, including those supplied by agencies and subcontractors where you are responsible. Employing someone without the right to work can lead to a civil penalty of up to £60,000 per worker, and action against your sponsor licence.

sections.heading: Sponsor licence for construction help in Manchester
sections.text: We're IAA-regulated and based in Manchester city centre, working with employers across the North West and the rest of the UK. We check which of your roles can be sponsored, prepare your sponsor licence application, and keep you compliant with our [sponsor licence compliance](/sponsor-licence-compliance/) service.

faqs.q: Can construction companies still sponsor tradespeople?
faqs.a: Only for trades on the temporary shortage list, which runs until 31 December 2026 unless extended. Engineers and other degree-level roles can still be sponsored.

faqs.q: Can sponsored tradespeople bring their families?
faqs.a: Workers newly sponsored in temporary shortage list roles below degree level can’t bring dependants. Degree-level roles can.
The government is deciding which occupations stay on the list. We follow the changes and will advise you on your roles.

faqs.q: How long does a sponsor licence application take?
faqs.a: The Home Office aims to decide most applications within 8 weeks. A priority service, when places are available, can get a decision faster for an extra fee. We prepare your documents first so the application isn't delayed by missing evidence.

faqs.q: Are we responsible for checking agency and subcontractor workers?
faqs.a: You must check the right to work of anyone you employ directly. For agency and subcontracted workers, make sure your contracts require those checks, and keep evidence, because enforcement visits often look at everyone on site.
